item.title: Senegal's first elite girls' boarding school challenges patriarchal norms
item.description: Off the coast of Dakar, Goree Island is home to the Senegal’s first elite boarding school for girls. item.title: European wild boars escaped a North Carolina hunting ranch in 1912; a century later...
item.description: Invasive European wild boars, originally introduced to the area in 1912, are wreaking havoc within Great Smoky Mountains National Park. To mitigate damage to delicate ecosystems, park management annually removes around 275 of these feral hogs. The boars breed with domestic pigs, creating hybrid species that further disrupt native wildlife. Efforts to control their population involve trapping, shooting, and implementing fencing strategies. item.description: Himalayan tahr were introduced to New Zealand's South Island by British aristocrats in pursuit of sport hunting back in 1904. Quickly multiplying, these creatures turned into an invasive species, wreaking havoc on native alpine ecosystems. Control measures, including government-led aerial shooting, have not proven entirely effective, creating a challenging situation for conservationists and hunters alike. The management of tahr remains an ongoing struggle within New Zealand's wildlife strategy. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
